title: Quadrature, root finding and error budgets

objectives.text: Derive a composite trapezoid approximation and its smooth-function discretization/evaluation error budget with explicit units and reference checks.
Maintain a continuous sign-changing bisection bracket and derive a midpoint location bound, separating residual magnitude, uncertain signs and iteration-budget status.

blocks.markdown: The definite integral I=integral_a^b f(x)dx is the limit of weighted sums over increasingly fine partitions when that limit exists. For continuous f on a finite closed interval it exists. It measures signed accumulation, with units(output of f)*(input x). Integrating a rate in currency/day over days gives currency, not another rate. Here a≤b are ordered finite endpoints; a=b gives zero accumulation. Stating a numerical integral does not establish that f models the intended process or that its inputs were available at decision time.

Split [a,b] into n equal panels of width h=(b-a)/n, with x_j=a+jh. Linearly interpolate f between adjacent nodes and integrate each line: panel contribution is h*(f(x_j)+f(x_{j+1}))/2. Adding panels gives T_n=h*[f(a)/2+sum_{j=1}^{n-1}f(x_j)+f(b)/2]. Interior nodes appear in two adjacent half-weighted panels; endpoints appear once. This derivation explains the weights rather than treating them as arbitrary constants.

Assume f has continuous second derivative and |f''|≤M on [a,b]. On one panel [u,u+h], interpolation error is f(x)-L(x)=f''(ξ_x)*(x-u)*(x-u-h)/2. Its absolute integral is at most (M/2)*integral_0^h t*(h-t)dt=M*h³/12. Sum n panels to get |I-T_n|≤(b-a)*M*h²/12. This is an upper bound, not an exact error or universal observed rate. Extra cancellation can improve some functions; nonsmooth/singular cases may not satisfy this bound at all.

blocks.caption: Expected lines: 1 1/2 1/6 True; 2 3/8 1/24 True; 4 11/32 1/96 True. The exact integral of x² over [0,1] is 1/3. Here f''=2 and the trapezoid overestimate exactly equals the bound 1/(6n²). This bounded int/Fraction helper intentionally integrates only x²; it does not claim adaptive or general-purpose quadrature.

blocks.markdown: If each function value at its exact intended node has absolute error at most η, the positive trapezoid weights sum to b-a. Thus evaluation perturbation contributes at most (b-a)*η. Combine this with discretization as |I-computed_T|≤(b-a)*M*h²/12+(b-a)*η, before adding any separately analyzed node-rounding/summation or model error. Making n larger does not remove the evaluation-error floor. The exact polynomial example avoids these numerical terms only within its stated rational model.

A root r satisfies f(r)=0. If f is continuous on [a,b] and endpoint values have opposite signs, the intermediate value theorem guarantees at least one root. An exact endpoint zero can be returned immediately. Continuity matters: a step jumping from -1 to +1 can have a sign change but no zero. A pole inside a bracket also breaks continuity. Conversely, f(x)=x² has a root at 0 without a sign change around it, so no sign bracket is not proof that no root exists.

For continuous opposite-sign endpoints, evaluate m=(a+b)/2. If f(m)=0 exactly, finish. Otherwise replace the endpoint having the same sign as f(m), retaining an opposite-sign half and therefore at least one root. Each replacement halves width. After k replacements, W_k=(b-a)/2^k, and the CURRENT bracket midpoint has distance at most W_k/2 from a root in that bracket. To request absolute location error≤tol, require W_k/2≤tol, not merely a small f(midpoint). Continuity and reliable signs are part of this reasoning; uniqueness needs additional information such as strict monotonicity.

blocks.title: Track the bracket, then its midpoint error

steps.text: For f(x)=x²-2 on [1,2], continuity and strict increase for x≥0 give exactly one nonnegative root. Initial values -1 and 2 have opposite signs.
m=3/2 has f(m)=1/4>0, so bracket becomes [1,3/2]. Its NEW midpoint is 5/4 with guaranteed location error≤1/4; the evaluated old midpoint 3/2 is now an endpoint, not that new midpoint.
Next m=5/4 has f(m)=-7/16<0, giving [5/4,3/2], new midpoint 11/8 and error≤1/8. Third m=11/8 has f(m)=-7/64<0, giving [11/8,3/2], new midpoint 23/16 and error≤1/16.
Distinguish evaluation count, replacement count, current bracket and the particular estimate returned. A budget cap may preserve a valid bracket while failing the requested tolerance.

blocks.source:
from fractions import Fraction
# Fixed continuous f(x)=x*x-2 has one nonnegative root, initially in[1,2].
lower,upper = Fraction(1),Fraction(2)
for iteration in range(1,4):
    midpoint = (lower+upper)/2
    if midpoint*midpoint < 2:
        lower = midpoint
    else:
        upper = midpoint
    print(iteration,str(lower),str(upper),str((upper-lower)/2))
print(lower*lower <= 2 <= upper*upper)
# A tiny residual can coexist with large location error.
print(Fraction(1,10**12)*(0-100),100)
blocks.caption: Expected lines: 1 1 3/2 1/4; 2 5/4 3/2 1/8; 3 11/8 3/2 1/16; True; then -1/10000000000 100. This is a fixed three-step trace, not a generic root API. For g(x)=1e-12*(x-100), g(0) has tiny magnitude 1e-10 while root-location error is 100. Rescaling function values changes residuals but not roots.

blocks.markdown: If a function evaluation has a CERTIFIED absolute error bound η, its sign is established only when the whole interval [value-η,value+η] lies strictly above or below zero. An interval containing zero has an indeterminate sign; refine the inner computation or report uncertainty instead of choosing a bisection half as though the sign were known. A quadrature routine's reported error ESTIMATE is not automatically a certified enclosure. Root finding around an approximate inner integral needs an explicit combined error policy.

Record absolute/relative location tolerances, iteration/evaluation budgets, returned bracket/estimate, residual and stop reason. In floating arithmetic also detect midpoint==endpoint or nonfinite values rather than looping forever or declaring exactness from a rounded zero. Library algorithms such as Brent combine bracketing/interpolation but retain continuity/sign assumptions. SciPy quad calls its abserr an estimate; a requested tolerance is not model truth or unconditional proof. These lessons do not claim SciPy availability in the app.

Independent transfer: integrate a linear function with the trapezoid formula and explain exactness when f''=0. Derive the fourfold quadratic-error reduction when n doubles and state the smoothness/evaluation assumptions. Build a discontinuous sign-change counterexample and an even root without a sign change. Finally calculate how many halvings shrink an initial width 8 to a midpoint error at most 1/8: W_k/2=4/2^k≤1/8 requires k≥5.

References: [composite Newton-Cotes formula](https://yaningliucudenver.github.io/Numerical-Analysis-I/bookchapter5-2.html), [MIT error/cancellation notes](https://math.mit.edu/~stevenj/trapezoidal.pdf), [FNC bracket proof](https://fncbook.com/python/secant/), [root conditioning](https://fncbook.com/rootproblem/), [bisection tolerance/status contract](https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/generated/scipy.optimize.bisect.html), and [quadrature error estimates](https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/generated/scipy.integrate.quad.html). Own exact model examples are not generic floating numerical certification.

summary: Quadrature needs weights, units and a smoothness/evaluation error budget. A continuous reliable sign bracket bounds root location through its width; tiny residuals, requested tolerances and error estimates have different meanings.
